title: Lost in Translation, Found in Laughter: The Joy of Cross-Cultural Encounters
title_zh: 迷失在翻译中，收获在笑声里：跨文化邂逅的乐趣
intro_zh: 本文约950词，围绕跨文化交流的乐趣展开，包含6个标注重点词和4道阅读理解题。

paragraphs.en: The alarm clock screamed at six in the morning, but I had already been lying awake for an hour, my stomach turning with nervous excitement. In a few hours I would leave my small city in China for a three-week international youth camp in Turkey. My spoken English was poor, my knowledge of foreign customs was poorer, and the only thing I carried with confidence was a pack of dumpling-shaped biscuits from my mother. Little did I know that this trip would become my most delightful lesson in cross-cultural encounters.
paragraphs.zh: 闹钟在早上六点尖叫起来，但我已经醒着躺了一个小时，胃里因紧张兴奋而翻腾。几个小时后，我将离开中国的小城市，前往土耳其参加为期三周的国际青年营。我的英语口语很差，对外国习俗的了解更差，唯一自信带着的是一包妈妈包的饺子形饼干。我完全不知道，这次旅行将成为我跨文化相遇中最愉快的一课。

paragraphs.en: Our camp brought together twenty-two students from countries as far apart as Brazil, Japan, Egypt, and Germany. On the first evening, each person had to introduce a typical dish from home in two minutes. A girl from Mexico placed crunchy tacos on the table, while a boy from Ghana brought a spicy peanut stew. When my turn came, I tried to explain the history of dumplings, but my broken English turned it into a comedy show. Everybody laughed at my wild hand gestures, and I laughed with them. At that moment, I realized that cross-cultural communication was not about perfect language, but about the willingness to misinterpret each other and laugh about it.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的营地聚集了来自巴西、日本、埃及、德国等国遥远各地的22名学生。第一晚，每个人要用两分钟介绍一道家乡特色菜。一个墨西哥女孩把脆脆的墨西哥卷饼放在桌上，一个加纳男孩带来了一锅辣花生炖菜。轮到我时，我试图解释饺子的历史，但蹩脚的英语把它变成了喜剧秀。大家都被我夸张的手势逗笑，我也跟着笑。那一刻我明白，跨文化交流不在于完美的语言，而在于愿意互相误解并对此一笑置之。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, we attended a workshop on cultural values. The trainer wrote two words on the board: time and relationship. She asked us, If a friend is thirty minutes late for a lunch meeting, what do you think? Students from Germany and Sweden raised their hands immediately: They should have called. It is disrespectful. However, students from Brazil and China shrugged: That is normal. The meeting does not begin until everyone feels comfortable. This was not just a debate about punctuality; it revealed how different cultures interpret the same action. Instead of judging one side as wrong, the trainer asked us to see each view as a piece of a larger puzzle. I began to understand that culture is not a barrier but a window into other ways of life.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天上午，我们参加了一场关于文化价值观的工作坊。培训师在黑板上写了两个词：时间和人际关系。她问我们：‘如果朋友午餐会迟到三十分钟，你会怎么想？’来自德国和瑞典的学生立刻举手：‘他们应该打电话，这是不礼貌的。’然而来自巴西和中国的学生耸耸肩：‘这很正常，要等大家都舒服了，会议才开始。’这不仅仅是关于守时的争论；它揭示了不同文化如何解读同一个行为。培训师没有评判哪一方错误，而是让我们把每种观点看作一块更大的拼图。我开始明白，文化不是障碍，而是通往其他生活方式的一扇窗。

paragraphs.en: Later in the week, we were invited to a local Turkish family for dinner. Our hosts placed a huge plate of rice, grilled meat, and salads in the center of the table. They insisted that we eat with our hands, using pieces of bread to pick up food. At first, I felt awkward and feared making a mess. But after watching a teenager from Morocco skillfully roll his rice into a small ball, I tried the same. To my surprise, the food tasted even better, and the laughter around the table broke down every invisible wall. The key was to be willing to adapt and try something foreign, not to prove that our own way was better.
paragraphs.zh: 后来那一周，我们受邀到当地一个土耳其家庭吃晚餐。主人在桌子中央放了一大盘米饭、烤肉和沙拉。他们坚持让我们用手抓食物，用面包片去拿。起初我觉得尴尬，害怕弄得到处都是。但看到来自摩洛哥的少年熟练地把米饭滚成小球，我也试了试。令我惊讶的是，食物尝起来更美味，桌边的笑声也打破了每堵看不见的墙。关键是要愿意去适应和尝试陌生的东西，而不是证明自己的方式更好。

paragraphs.en: One afternoon, we played a team-building game that required us to guide a blindfolded partner through an obstacle course using only a foreign language phrase we had just learned. My partner was a girl from South Korea, and I had to shout the Korean word for left while she shouted the Chinese word for forward. We failed many times, but every mistake made us laugh. When we finally crossed the finish line, we hugged like old friends. This experience taught me an important truth: communication breakdowns are temporary, but embarrassment and laughter can quickly become a shared language. In fact, research shows that when people experience communication challenges together, their trust grows faster than when everything goes smoothly.
paragraphs.zh: 一天下午，我们玩了一个团建游戏，要求只用刚学的一句外语引导蒙住眼睛的同伴穿越障碍赛道。我的搭档是一个韩国女孩，我必须用韩语喊‘左’，而她用中文喊‘前进’。我们失败了很多次，但每次错误都让我们发笑。当我们终于跨过终点线时，我们像老朋友一样拥抱。这段经历教会我一个重要的道理：沟通上的破裂是暂时的，但尴尬和笑声能迅速变成一种共同语言。事实上，研究表明，当人们一同经历沟通挑战时，他们的信任比一切顺利时增长得更快。

paragraphs.en: The most powerful moment came during a culture night performance. Each country group prepared a three-minute show to introduce their culture. My team chose the Chinese folk song Mo Li Hua. But when I sang it in an old, local style, some of my African friends began to dance freely to the beat, adding new rhythms that I had never imagined. At first, I was worried that they were ruining the song. Then I realized they were not ruining it; they were embracing it with their own cultural voice. The song became something new and beautiful, and everyone in the room felt the joy of co-creation. That night, I saw how culture can be enriched when we allow others to add their colors to our canvas.
paragraphs.zh: 最震撼的时刻发生在文化之夜表演上。每个国家小组准备一个三分钟的节目来介绍自己的文化。我们组选了中文民歌《茉莉花》。但我用老式本土风格演唱时，一些非洲朋友开始随着节拍自由起舞，加上了我从未想象过的新节奏。起初我担心他们在毁掉这首歌。然后我意识到，他们不是在毁掉它，而是在用自己的文化之声拥抱它。这首歌变成了全新而美好的东西，房间里的每个人都感受到了共同创作的快乐。那一夜，我看到当我们允许别人往我们的画布上增添色彩时，文化会变得丰富。

paragraphs.en: According to a survey by the European Youth Forum, 78 percent of young people who participate in international exchange programs say they become more open-minded and patient after the experience. Another study from the University of California found that people who regularly interact with different cultures are better at creative problem-solving. My own ten days in Turkey were far too short, but they stretched my view of the world in a way that no textbook could. I learned to appreciate the little differences, from the way greetings vary in different countries to the different meanings of silence.
paragraphs.zh: 根据欧洲青年论坛的一项调查，78%参加过国际交流项目的年轻人表示，他们事后变得更为开放和耐心。加州大学的一项研究也发现，经常与不同文化互动的人在创造性解决问题方面更出色。我在土耳其的短短十天虽然太短，但却以任何教科书都无法做到的方式扩展了我的世界观。我学会了欣赏微小的差异——从各国问候方式的不同，到沉默在不同文化中的含义。

paragraphs.en: Now, whenever someone asks me why I love traveling, I do not talk about famous buildings or beautiful beaches. I talk about clumsy conversations at dinner tables and the bursts of laughter when someone misunderstands a word. Cross-cultural communication is not a skill to be perfected; it is a playground where we fall, rise, and laugh together. The real joy lies not in becoming fluent in many languages, but in becoming fluent in humanity.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，每当有人问我为什么喜欢旅行时，我谈论的不是著名建筑或美丽海滩，而是餐桌上的笨拙对话，以及有人误解一个词时爆发的笑声。跨文化交流不是一种需要臻于完美的技能，而是一个我们跌倒、爬起、共同大笑的游乐园。真正的乐趣不在于能流利地说多种语言，而在于能够流畅地理解人性。

questions.q: What is the author's main purpose in writing this passage?
options: To explain why cross-cultural communication is difficult and frustrating.
To share personal experiences that show cross-cultural communication can be joyful and rewarding.
To persuade readers to study foreign languages before traveling.
To describe the history and culture of Turkey.
questions.explain: 文章通过作者在国际青年营的亲身经历，展示了跨文化中的误会和笑话如何带来乐趣与成长，因此主要目的是分享经历，说明跨文化交流很有趣且有益。

questions.q: Why did the author initially feel worried when some African friends danced to Mo Li Hua?
options: She thought they would hurt themselves.
She thought they were disrespecting her culture.
She thought they were ruining the song.
She thought the show would be too long.
questions.explain: 第六段明确说‘I was worried that they were ruining the song’，所以作者担心他们破坏了歌曲。

questions.q: What does the author imply about cultural differences in the article?
options: They always lead to serious conflicts.
They can be a source of laughter and deeper understanding.
They disappear when people speak the same language.
They should be avoided as much as possible.
questions.explain: 从全文多处例子（手抓饭、迟到讨论、舞蹈加入等）可以看出文化差异可以变成笑声和相互理解的桥梁，而非冲突。

questions.q: The word 'embracing' in paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to:
questions.explain: 此处‘embracing it with their own cultural voice’表示‘用自己的文化声音欣然接受它’，与hugging不同，C正确。
